messages:
jordan: Heads up — since last night's runtime change we're seeing a big missstorm on prefix cache for chat-route-3. Miss rate jumped from ~18% -> ~87% and backend QPS spiked 3x. p99 latency for small requests climbed from 120ms -> 680ms.
li: ugh. Any idea which change in the rollout? did we change hashing or kernel paths?
marta: I noticed the rollout toggled the new kernel selection heuristic + a tiny change in prefix hashing (murmur3 seed bumped to make the new sharding stable). could be a seed/namespace shift.
kevin: yeah the kernel selector moved some models to the "fast-int8" path which changes how we canonicalize the key (we added model_variant to the cache key). rollout notes: "include kernel_tag in cache key for safety" — that seemed fine in staging.
jordan: attaching quick sample from logs: 
```
kv_cache.lookup(prefix_hash=0x7f4a, key="chat-route-3|model-v2|kernel-fast-int8|<prompt>") -> MISS
kv_cache.lookup(prefix_hash=0xa1c3, key="chat-route-3|model-v2|kernel-x64|<prompt>") -> HIT
```
so same prefix text but kernel_tag flipped keys. That explains lost hits, but why a missstorm instead of graceful warmup?
li: because when a lot of requests change key namespace simultaneously we get thundering herd against the backing store. our cache LRU had just-evicted prefixes and the fallback causes concurrent backend fetches. no jitter on re-warm currently.
kevin: perf-bot: profiling snapshot at 02:14 UTC shows: 55% time in kv_miss_fetch (http backend), 20% in memcpy on CPU, 12% in kernel-launch overhead. nvprof shows increased kernel-greenlet scheduling but that's secondary.
perf-bot: ```
perf top summary:
  kv_miss_fetch_http 55.2%
  memcpy              20.1%
  kernel_launch       12.3%
  other               12.4%
```
marta: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) emergency flag to ignore kernel_tag in cache key for compatible variants (fast rollout) 2) enable per-prefix jittered backoff on miss fetch to avoid simultaneous backend calls 3) pre-warm most-hit prefixes for the new keyspace via synthetic warmup.
li: agree. option 1 is lowest risk. we need to ensure correctness — ignoring kernel_tag might serve responses produced with different kernel, but output should be bitwise same for these variants (we tested for this model).
kevin: I'll flip the emergency gate to revert cache key variant inclusion. can someone validate the model equivalence quickly?
jordan: quick A/B check on a sample set (10k requests) — outputs are within tolerances, no hallucination regressions. ok to proceed.
kevin: done. emergency gate toggled at 02:32 UTC. backend QPS back down to ~1.2x and miss rate down to 24% within 3m. p95 to p99 trending down.
marta: follow-up: we should backfill analytics to compute delta in effective cache hit-rate attributable to key changes vs eviction. I suspect ~65% of the new misses were pure key namespace shifts, 20% from eviction churn, 15% from tokenizer mismatches (whitespace/tokenizer differences across client SDK).
li: tokenizer bit is interesting — we saw a tiny change in how client strips trailing spaces in function-call payloads. that could produce different prefixes even with same logical prompt. add canonicalization layer.
kevin: action items: (a) roll out canonicalizer for prompt normalization (gzip canonical), (b) add per-key jittered fetch + small randomized exponential backoff, (c) implement warmup job that runs in background for top N prefixes when keyspace changes, (d) add a canary check in rollout pipeline that simulates cache hit-rate delta before flipping cache-key semantics.
jordan: I'll own (d) and (c) — will write a small runner that replays top prefixes into the new keyspace and measures hit-rate.
marta: I'll own (a) — plan: trim trailing whitespace, normalize JSON arguments ordering for function calls, collapse repeated whitespace, and canonicalize unicode normal form. patch + unit tests in prs today.
li: I'll own (b) and coordinate with SRE to tune backoff parameters. also propose a dashboard for cache key entropy + hit-rate by model+kernel_tag so we can detect this earlier.
oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged. Severity lowered to P2 after emergency gate toggle.
kevin: posting follow-up plan to #eng-releases and will coordinate a staged rollout with the canary step.
jordan: thanks all. we should run a short postmortem after metrics settle (24h). initial tl;dr: cache key expansion (kernel_tag) + simultaneous rollout produced namespace shift -> missstorm -> backend overload. mitigated by emergency key-gate and will follow up with canonicalization, jittered fetch, warmup, and canarying.
perf-bot: recording timeline: 02:14 detect -> 02:20 investigations -> 02:32 emergency toggle -> 02:35 partial recovery -> 03:00 stable.
kevin: will open postmortem doc and link perf traces. please paste any relevant logs or synthetic warmup scripts you write into that doc.
li: adding one more note: add unit tests in kernel selector CI to assert that changes that affect cache semantics must set "semantics-impact: true" in the rollout note.
jordan: agreed. will include that in postmortem.
marta: thanks — good catch from monitoring alerts. closing thread once postmortem is up.
